status_summary: The Fed's statutory mandate is unchanged, but a bill to remove the maximum-employment goal has cleared a House committee. H.R. 5396, the Price Stability Act (Rep. Hill, chairman of the House Financial Services Committee; introduced 2025-09-16), amends section 2A of the Federal Reserve Act to remove the employment goal while leaving the moderate long-term interest rates goal in place. The committee took up the bill in May 2026 (a bill-tracking site reports a 30 to 21 vote) and reported it with an amendment on 2026-06-24 (H. Rept. 119-710, Union Calendar No. 616); no House floor vote or Senate companion was found, and a CRS product of 2026-05-21 discusses only this bill. Separately, the FOMC reaffirmed its longer-run goals statement on 2026-01-27 with both maximum employment and price stability and a 2 percent goal; that statement, unchanged from August 2025, no longer contains averaging language, so the Fed itself dropped the flexible average inflation targeting approach the chapter wanted ended (an action by the Fed, not by elected officials). The FOMC's 2026-09-16 statement describes its rate increase as supporting the dual mandate. Kevin Warsh was sworn in as chair on 2026-05-22, and on 2026-07-09 the Fed announced task forces, including one on inflation frameworks. No statutory requirement for a published inflation target range and path was found.

timeline.event: Rep. Hill, with Reps. Stutzman and Donalds, introduces H.R. 5396, the Price Stability Act, which amends section 2A of the Federal Reserve Act to remove the maximum-employment goal; referred to the House Financial Services Committee. The committee's release of 2025-09-17 describes it as ending the dual mandate.
FOMC reaffirmed its Statement on Longer-Run Goals and Monetary Policy Strategy with text unchanged from August 2025 (reaffirmation at the annual organization meeting).

House Financial Services Committee takes up H.R. 5396 in markup (a bill tracker gives this date; a CRS In Focus dated 2026-05-21 says the committee marked it up in May 2026; the exact date of the committee vote was not confirmed).
Kevin Warsh sworn in as Fed chairman and Board member and selected as FOMC chairman; nominated 2026-03-04 and confirmed by the Senate 2026-05-12 (Board) and 2026-05-13 (chair).

H.R. 5396 reported with an amendment by the Committee on Financial Services (H. Rept. 119-710) and placed on the Union Calendar (No. 616); the reported version is titled the Price Stability Act of 2026.
Fed announced five task forces to review the conduct of monetary policy, including inflation frameworks (co-led by N. Gregory Mankiw, Thomas Sargent and William White) and communications.
FOMC statement raised the target range by 0.25 percentage point and described the action as supporting the Fed's dual mandate; vote 12 to 0.

title: End the Fed's dual mandate and make price stability its sole statutory objective
uncertainties: The committee vote count (30 to 21) and the 2026-05-13 markup date come from a bill-tracking site (simplefunctions.dev) that lists the vote on the 2026-06-24 reporting date; CRS and a legislative news site confirm only that the committee marked up and advanced the bill in May 2026, and the govinfo reported version confirms the 2026-06-24 report. The text retrieved from govinfo strikes only the employment term in section 2A, whereas the sponsor's release describes a single price stability mandate; how the bill treats the moderate long-term interest rate language was not resolved because the reported-version amendment text did not render. No floor vote or Senate companion was found, but congress.gov could not be read and the search budget did not allow a dedicated Senate search; CRS lists only this one bill. The earlier claim about Jackson Hole remarks in August 2026 was dropped because it rested on a Wikipedia summary that was not verified. The FOMC statement text itself was not re-read; the averaging-language point is carried from the earlier reviewer's check of the Fed's longer-run goals PDF.
